question: What will the EU aggregate gas storage filling level be for gas day 12 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Start: ~74.6% (845 TWh) on gas day 31 Oct per AGSI-derived trackers (Voltstack, EnergyRiskIQ); 12 gas days remain to 12 Nov. Reference class: EU 1-12 Nov changes 2021-2025 ranged ~+0.6 to -2.5 pp; cold/still Novembers (2021, 2024) drew 1.5-2.5 pp. Forecast cold snap (Germany 2-4C below normal, Dunkelflaute, possible SSW ~9 Nov) points to ~0.2-0.3 pp/day vs the recent ~0.13, giving a center near 72.0. Arguments for less drawdown: high TTF (~95-97 EUR/MWh) curbing demand and pulling in LNG, and third-party projections of ~71% only by 23 Nov. Below-68 would need ~0.55 pp/day sustained (~1%); above 77 has no mechanism. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold none per harness; Kalshi and bookmakers not checked).
calls.dossier:
- Voltstack Days-of-Gas (gas day 31 Oct 2026): EU 845 TWh, 74.6% of capacity; average net withdrawal over the past week only ~0.32 TWh/day; 1 pp ≈ 11.3 TWh (working gas volume 1,132.8 TWh).
- EnergyRiskIQ (page dated 2 Nov 2026): EU 74.6%, daily change shown as +0.10 pp vs prior day (gas day unclear, possibly stale); 15.4 pp below the seasonal norm of ~90%.
- Global-energy-flow: 74.93% on gas day 26 Oct (848.8 TWh); Germany 61.65%, NL 65.5%, France 87%, Italy 91%.
- Question background: 74.64% on 30 Oct, net withdrawal ~1.49 TWh/day (-0.13 pp/day); first net withdrawal of the season was 22 Oct (TokenPost, 27 Oct).
- EnergyConnects/Bloomberg (31 Oct 2026): Germany 61.17%, missed its ~70% 1 Nov target; cold snap forecast 2-4C below normal for Berlin/Frankfurt/Munich, possible frost in the south/east, Dunkelflaute (low wind/solar) raising gas-for-power burn.
- TokenPost (27 Oct 2026): TTF topped EUR 97/MWh on the cold forecast; temperatures 2-3C below normal from the weekend of 31 Oct/1 Nov; Asia also cold, so LNG competition.
- Background: ECMWF ensembles show a possible polar-vortex disturbance/wind reversal around 9 Nov; a third-party extrapolation puts the EU at ~71% by 23 Nov.
- Voltstack: average net withdrawal 1 Nov-31 Mar over winters 2016/17-2025/26 is 4.0 TWh/day (~0.35 pp/day); early November is typically well below that average.
- Historical 1-12 Nov EU changes (from memory, not verified this run): 2021 about -1.5 pp (low-storage year), 2022 about +0.5 (mild), 2023 about 0 (mild), 2024 about -2 (Dunkelflaute), 2025 small (withdrawals started mid-Nov).
- Pace arithmetic from 74.6 on 31 Oct over 12 days: -0.1/day -> 73.4; -0.2 -> 72.2; -0.3 -> 71.0; -0.4 -> 69.8.
- Status quo: a gradual decline from ~74.6.
- Resolution: resolves off the AGSI+ 'EU' dataset 'full' field for gas day 2026-11-12, first publication; not the 'Europe' aggregate; later revisions ignored.
- Event window: gas days 31 Oct -> 12 Nov 2026 matter (the latest known datapoint is 31 Oct); as of 2 Nov, about 2 of 13 days (~15%) have elapsed with no datapoints seen for 1-2 Nov.
- Searched but not found: AGSI+ data for 1-2 Nov (the API needs a key); detailed HDD forecasts for 5-12 Nov; any prediction market (none found on Polymarket/Manifold).
calls.reference_class: EU-aggregate AGSI+ storage change over 1-12 November, 2021-2025, conditioned on weather regime

calls.reasoning: Last confirmed AGSI+ EU value 74.64% (gas day 30 Oct, -0.13 pp/day). A cold snap (2-4°C below normal plus low-wind, low-solar conditions) began around 31 Oct, and ECMWF signals a polar-vortex disturbance around 9 Nov, so withdrawals should speed up from late-Oct's ~1.5 TWh/day. Early-November falls in past years (2021, 2024, 2025) ran about 0.17-0.3 pp/day. €95-100 TTF demand destruction and LNG inflows dampen the decline, and mild spells could pause it. Central estimate about 0.24 pp/day over 13 days gives ~71.5%. Below 68% requires >0.5 pp/day sustained (severe cold), priced at 3%. No human market found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers.

- Damping factors: high prices cut demand. ENTSOG winter outlook (8 Oct) judged the system flexible. Mild/windy days can bring near-zero or small net injection.
- Historical: early-November EU daily changes ranged from small injections to roughly -0.3 to -0.45 pp in cold, low-wind spells (e.g. Nov 2024). Typical first-half-Nov averages ~0.15-0.3 pp/d in 2021/2024/2025 (recall, not re-verified).

- Resolves off the AGSI+ 'EU' aggregate 'full' field, first publication for gas day 2026-11-12 (not the 'Europe' aggregate; later revisions ignored).

calls.reference_class: EU aggregate storage change over the first ~13 days of the withdrawal season (late Oct to mid Nov), 2021-2025 AGSI+

Reference class: EU net withdrawals in early-to-mid November 2021-25, roughly 0.15-0.35 pp/day (about 0.4 pp/day in the Nov 2024 Dunkelflaute), which implies about 70-73% on 12 Nov. calls.reasoning: Starts at ~74.6% (30-31 Oct), with net withdrawals beginning. A cold, low-wind/low-solar spell in Germany (2-4C below normal) and an ECMWF polar-vortex signal around 9 Nov point to draws of ~0.2-0.3 pp/day, faster than late October's -0.13. Very high TTF (~95-100 EUR/MWh) curbs demand and pulls in LNG, damping the fall. Central path is -0.25 pp/day over 12 days, giving ~71.6%. calls.reconciliation: Factual: start level 74.6% on both 30 and 31 Oct, so the runs agree; Voltstack's 0.32 TWh/day weekly average vs the 1.49 TWh/day AGSI daily figure is explained by injection days earlier in the window; EnergyRiskIQ's +0.10 pp is likely stale and was down-weighted. No web access this run, so post-30-Oct AGSI values were unverified. Judgment: in a cold, still spell with storage low, the pace should run harder than late October's but be damped by price-driven demand cuts; I took -0.25 pp/day. My median sits near Runs 2 and 3; the lower-tail escape is set at 2%.
